Setting $j^-_\varepsilon=\min\{j: \varepsilon j\in I_\varepsilon^{k_\varepsilon^-}\}$ and $j^+_\varepsilon=\max\{j: \varepsilon j\in J_\varepsilon^{k_\varepsilon^+}\}$, we define $\hat u^{\varepsilon}$ by setting 
\begin{equation}\label{def-costante}
\hat u^{\varepsilon}_i=\left\{ \begin{array}{ll}
u^\varepsilon_{j^-_\varepsilon} & \hbox{ if } i\leq  j^-_\varepsilon \\
u^\varepsilon_i &  \hbox{ if } j^-_\varepsilon \leq i\leq j^+_\varepsilon  \\
u^\varepsilon_{j^+_\varepsilon} &  \hbox{ if } i\geq j^+_\varepsilon.
\end{array}
\right. 
\end{equation}
Since $j_\varepsilon^{-}\geq L\varepsilon^{-\alpha}$ and $j_\varepsilon^{+}\leq N_\varepsilon-L\varepsilon^{-\alpha}$, then $\hat u^\varepsilon$ satisfies claim (i). Moreover, $\hat u^\varepsilon\to u$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$. To prove this, for simplicity we suppose that $m_n$ is not increasing for $n\geq 1$. Then,  
\begin{eqnarray*}\varepsilon\sum_{i=1}^{j^-_\varepsilon}(u^\varepsilon_i-\hat u^\varepsilon_{i})^2&=&\varepsilon\sum_{i=1}^{j^-_\varepsilon}(u^\varepsilon_i-u^\varepsilon_{j^-_\varepsilon})^2\leq \varepsilon\sum_{i=1}^{j^-_\varepsilon} j^-_\varepsilon \!\!\sum_{j=i+1}^{j^-_\varepsilon}\!(u^\varepsilon_i-u^\varepsilon_{i-1})^2\\
&\leq& \frac{S}{m_1}\varepsilon^2 (j^-_\varepsilon)^2\leq \frac{S}{m_1}\lambda_\varepsilon^2,\end{eqnarray*}
and correspondingly $\varepsilon\sum_{i=j^+_\varepsilon}^{\lfloor L/\varepsilon\rfloor}(u^\varepsilon_i-\hat u^\varepsilon_{i})^2\leq \frac{S}{m_1}\lambda_\varepsilon^2$.
Setting, $n_\varepsilon=\lfloor\frac{\lambda_\varepsilon}{\varepsilon (M_\varepsilon+1)}\rfloor$, since 
$$\sum_{|i-j|\geq n_\varepsilon} m_{|i-j|}(u^{\varepsilon}_i-u^{\varepsilon}_j)^2 \leq 
\frac{2}{\varepsilon}  m_{n_\varepsilon} \|u^\varepsilon\|^2_{L_2}\leq 
\frac{2}{\varepsilon}  m_{\lfloor\varepsilon^{-\alpha}\rfloor} \|u^\varepsilon\|^2_{L_2},$$
and recalling  \eqref{stimaM1}, we obtain 
\begin{eqnarray*} 
F_\varepsilon(\hat u^{\varepsilon};[0,L])\leq F_\varepsilon(u^{\varepsilon};[0,L])+ 2\lambda_\varepsilon f(0) + \frac{C}{\varepsilon^2} 
m_{\lfloor\varepsilon^{-\alpha}\rfloor}+\frac{C}{M_\varepsilon},
\end{eqnarray*}
where 
$C$ denotes a constant depending only on $\sup_\varepsilon F_\varepsilon(u^\varepsilon;[0,L])$ and $\sup_\varepsilon\|u^\varepsilon\|_{L^2}$.  
Setting 
$$r(t)=2f(0) t^{\alpha^\prime}+Ct^{\alpha\beta-2}+C t^{1-\alpha-\alpha^\prime},$$
we conclude the proof since $m_n=o(n^{-\beta})$ and $\alpha>\frac{2}{\beta}$.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{boundarycond2} 
Let $L>0$ and $N_\varepsilon=\lfloor\frac{L}{\varepsilon}\rfloor$. 
Let $\alpha\in(\frac{2}{\beta},1)$. 
Assume that $u^\varepsilon, v^\varepsilon\in \mathcal A_\varepsilon$ be such that (the piecewise-affine extensions of) 
$u^\varepsilon$ and $v^\varepsilon$ converge to $u$ in $L^2(0,L)$ and $\sup_\varepsilon (E_\varepsilon(u^\varepsilon;[0,L])+\|u^\varepsilon\|^2_{L^2})=S<+\infty$. Then there exist $\hat u^{\varepsilon}, \hat v^\varepsilon \in \mathcal A_\varepsilon$ converging to $u$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\rm(i)}] $\hat u^\varepsilon_i=\hat v^\varepsilon_i=\hat u^\varepsilon_0$ for $i\leq \varepsilon^{-\alpha}$,  $\hat u^\varepsilon_i=\hat v^\varepsilon_i=\hat u^\varepsilon_{N_\varepsilon}$ 
for $i\geq N_\varepsilon-\varepsilon^{-\alpha}$; 
\item[{\rm(ii)}] $E_\varepsilon(\hat u^\varepsilon, \hat v^\varepsilon;[0,L])\leq E_\varepsilon(u^\varepsilon, v^\varepsilon;[0,L])+r(\varepsilon)$, where the remainder $r$ depends only on $S$ and $f(0)$, and $r(\varepsilon)\to 0$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$.  
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
We choose $\lambda_\varepsilon$ and $M_\varepsilon$ as in the proof of Lemma \ref{boundarycond}, 
and divide $(0,\lambda_\varepsilon]$ and $[L-\lambda_\varepsilon,L)$ in $M_\varepsilon+1$ intervals, denoted by $I^k_\varepsilon$ and $J^k_\varepsilon$ respectively, as above. 
Then, there exist $k_\varepsilon$ and $h_\varepsilon$ in $\{1,\dots, M_\varepsilon\}$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{stimaM3}
\frac{1}{2\varepsilon} \sum_{\varepsilon i\in I_\varepsilon^{k_\varepsilon}\cup J_\varepsilon^{h_\varepsilon}} \big(a(v^\varepsilon_i-v^\varepsilon_{i-1})^2+b(u^\varepsilon_i-v^\varepsilon_{i})^2 \big)
\leq \frac{S}{M_\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}
Setting $j^-_\varepsilon=\min\{j: \varepsilon j\in I_\varepsilon^{k_\varepsilon}\}$ and $j^+_\varepsilon=\max\{j: \varepsilon j\in J_\varepsilon^{h_\varepsilon}\}$, we define 
\begin{equation*}
\hat u^{\varepsilon}_i=\left\{ \begin{array}{ll}
u^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-} & \hbox{ if } i\leq  j_{\varepsilon}^- \\
u^\varepsilon_i &  \hbox{ if } j_{\varepsilon}^-< i<  j_{\varepsilon}^+ \\
u^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^+} &  \hbox{ if } i\geq  j_{\varepsilon}^+
\end{array}
\right. 
\ \ 
\hbox{ and } \ \ \ \
\hat v^{\varepsilon}_i=\left\{ \begin{array}{ll}
u^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-} & \hbox{ if } i\leq j_{\varepsilon}^- \\
v^\varepsilon_i &  \hbox{ if } j_{\varepsilon}^-< i <  j_{\varepsilon}^+ \\
u^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^+} &  \hbox{ if } i\geq j_{\varepsilon}^+,
\end{array}
\right. 
\end{equation*}
so that $\hat u^\varepsilon$ and $\hat v^\varepsilon$ converge to $u$ in $L^2$, 
and satisfy (i). Recalling \eqref{stimaM3}, we get 
in particular that 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\frac{a}{2\varepsilon} (\hat v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-+1}-\hat v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-})^2\leq 
\frac{a}{\varepsilon} (v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-+1}-v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-})^2+ \frac{a}{\varepsilon} (v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-}-u^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-})^2 
\leq \frac{C}{M_\varepsilon},
\end{eqnarray*}
where $C$ denotes a positive constant depending only on $a,b$ and $S$. 
The same bound holds for $\frac{a}{2\varepsilon}(\hat v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^+}-\hat v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^+-1})^2$. 
Hence 
\begin{eqnarray*}
E_\varepsilon(\hat u_\varepsilon,\hat v_\varepsilon; [0,L])&\leq&
2\lambda_\varepsilon f(0)
+E_\varepsilon(u^\varepsilon,v^\varepsilon;(0,L)) \\
&&
+\frac{a}{2\varepsilon} (\hat v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-+1}-\hat v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^-})^2
+
\frac{a}{2\varepsilon}(\hat v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^+}-\hat v^\varepsilon_{j_{\varepsilon}^+-1})^2
\\
&\leq&
2\lambda_\varepsilon f(0)
+E_\varepsilon(u^\varepsilon,v^\varepsilon;[0,L]) + \frac{2C}{M_\varepsilon},
\end{eqnarray*}
concluding the proof as above.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- remark-59: body_md -->
\label{rem-bound}\rm In the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{boundarycond2}, 
if there exists $\alpha\in (0,1)$ such that 
$u^\varepsilon_i=\hat u^\varepsilon_0$ for $i\leq \varepsilon^{-\alpha}$ and $u^\varepsilon_i=\hat u^\varepsilon_{N_\varepsilon}$ for $i\geq N_\varepsilon-\varepsilon^{-\alpha}$ for some $\alpha>0$, 
then the function $\hat v^\varepsilon$ can be chosen such that 
it coincides with $u^\varepsilon$ for $i\leq \varepsilon^{-\alpha^{\prime\prime}}$ and for $i\geq N_\varepsilon-\varepsilon^{-\alpha^{\prime\prime}}$ with $\alpha^{\prime\prime}<\alpha$.
<!-- end remark-59 -->
